subject: FinTech Corp RFI: Transparency portfolio declaration and evidence bundle
messages:
From: Sanjay Reddy <sanjay.reddy@fintechcorp.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood-inference.com
Cc: procurement@fintechcorp.com
Date: 2028-07-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFI: Vendor transparency & subprocessor evidence request

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week — the platform looks promising. Procurement is running a standard RFI ahead of our vendor selection and we need a concise package focused on third-party operators and controls. Can you share the following by EOD next Friday (Aug 4)?

- Current subprocessor roster (names, primary function, regions of operation)
- Confirmation of cloud providers used per region and fallback policy
- Most recent SOC 2 report and evidence of encryption-in-transit/e2e network diagrams
- Any planned subprocessor changes in the next 90 days (or change notification window)
- Point of contact for security/third-party due diligence follow-ups

We can sign an NDA if needed. Procurement will consolidate multiple vendor packages and follow up with any clarifying questions.

Best,
Sanjay Reddy
Senior Procurement Manager
FinTech Corp

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood-inference.com>
To: Sanjay Reddy <sanjay.reddy@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: rafael.mendes@redwood-inference.com, ben.carter@redwood-inference.com
Date: 2028-07-30T10:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Vendor transparency & subprocessor evidence request

Hi Sanjay — thanks for outlining the list. We can provide a consolidated evidence bundle by Aug 4. I'm looping in Rafael (legal) and Ben (security) to assemble the artifacts and confirm the change-notice windows.

A couple quick clarifying items so we can prioritize:
- Do you need the full historic roster (3+ years) or current + planned only?
- Any specific compliance artifacts beyond SOC 2 (ISO, PCI, etc.) we should include?

We can also send a short statement describing our notification process for subprocessor changes. If procurement prefers an in-person walk-through, I'm available for a 30-min call next week.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood-inference.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood-inference.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood-inference.com, ben.carter@redwood-inference.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood-inference.com
Date: 2028-07-31T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: FW: RFI: Vendor transparency & subprocessor evidence request

Kimberly / Ben — drafting the legal cover note and preparing the SOC 2 attachment. Key points to include in the cover letter:

- Redwood maintains a published subprocessor roster (current) and offers a 30-day notification window for material additions; critical/emergency operator changes are communicated immediately to named contacts.
- Data residency commitments are configurable per-customer via Regions in the Console; our contractual obligations and SLAs are spelled out in the Dedicated/Private addenda.
- SOC 2 Type II report (period ending 2027-12-31) attached. We should redact test-control detail but include assertion and scope.

Attachment: SOC2-Type2-Redwood-2027.pdf (redacted copy)

Draft paragraph for notification cadence:

"Redwood commits to notifying impacted customers of planned subprocessor changes at least 30 calendar days prior to the effective date. In cases of operational emergency (e.g., security incident or forced migration), Redwood will provide immediate notification and a mitigation plan, including fallbacks to alternative providers and region-level failover where applicable."

I'll prepare a concise legal cover letter for procurement to sign off. Ben — please add any technical assurances regarding network topology and encryption we should attach.

Regards,
Rafael Mendes
Legal Counsel | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood-inference.com, kimberly.park@redwood-inference.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood-inference.com
Date: 2028-08-02T08:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Vendor transparency & subprocessor evidence request

Adding technical attachments and a short technical assurance note. Points to include:

- Primary cloud providers: AWS (us-east-1, us-west-2) for hosted and Dedicated, with GCP used for certain analytics workloads in us-central1. We do not use consumer cloud providers for production data.
- Fallback policy: Requests are routed by policy: preferred region -> alternate region (same provider) -> alternate provider in the same legal jurisdiction; we maintain tested runbooks for failover.
- Encryption: TLS 1.2+ in transit, customer data at rest encrypted with KMS keys (customer-managed keys available for Private deployments).
- Network diagram attached (network-diagram-redwood.png) showing Console control plane separation and customer data path.
- Subprocessor roster attached as CSV (subprocessor_inventory_2028.csv) with vendor name, purpose, region, and typical access scope.

Note on change notices: Operationally we classify changes as: routine (30-day notice), scheduled (planned migrations, 14-30 day window), and emergency (as Rafael noted; immediate notification + mitigation). For procurement scoring, we typically offer a statement of intent and an evidence bundle rather than raw logs.

Ben Carter
Head of Security & Trust | Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood-inference.com>
To: Sanjay Reddy <sanjay.reddy@fintechcorp.com>, procurement@fintechcorp.com
Cc: rafael.mendes@redwood-inference.com, ben.carter@redwood-inference.com, laura.bennett@redwood-inference.com
Date: 2028-08-04T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Vendor transparency & subprocessor evidence request

Hi Sanjay / Procurement Team — attached is the consolidated package per your list.

Attachments included:
- subprocessor_inventory_2028.csv (current roster; columns: vendor, role, region, access-scope)
- SOC2-Type2-Redwood-2027.pdf (redacted copy for procurement review)
- network-diagram-redwood.png (high-level network and control plane diagram)

We have also placed the full evidence bundle in a shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-fintech-rfi

A few summary bullets for your scoring:
- Notification: 30-day standard notification for routine additions; emergency notifications are immediate and include migration/rollback options.
- Regions & Providers: Primary providers are AWS (us-east-1, us-west-2) and GCP (us-central1 for analytics). Customers may opt for Dedicated/Private to enforce region-only processing.
- Controls: SOC 2 Type II in scope for security and availability; TLS encryption in transit and KMS-based encryption at rest. Private deployments support customer-managed keys.

If procurement would like a short walkthrough of the folder and attachments, I'm happy to book a 30-minute call next week. Rafael and Ben are available to join for any follow-up control questions.

Thanks — Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood-inference.com | +1 415-555-0192
